dhcp_server_disclosure.title: DHCP Server Discovered on Local Subnet
dhcp_server_disclosure.description: A DHCP server responded to a broadcast DHCPDISCOVER on the agent's local subnet. The server's IP and the offered IP are visible to all clients on the subnet.
dhcp_server_disclosure.impact: Informational on managed networks. On guest/IoT segments, a rogue DHCP server can be used to redirect traffic (DHCP starvation + spoofing). Confirms one of: (a) the expected DHCP server, (b) a rogue DHCP server (red flag), (c) an old/forgotten DHCP service on a server that shouldn't be one.
dhcp_server_disclosure.remediation: Verify the discovered server IP matches the network operator's expected DHCP server. If not, investigate the rogue DHCP source (e.g., a Windows server with the DHCP role accidentally enabled, or an attacker's box). Enable DHCP snooping at the switch level to prevent rogue DHCP attacks.
dhcp_server_disclosure.evidence_template: Broadcast DHCPDISCOVER returned offer from server {{server_ip}}: offered IP {{offered_ip}}.
